input.name: Notes Improver
input.description: Once a day, look at how many notes files the project gained and propose one concrete way to add more of them per day, so the Notes Files stock rises.
invariants: It never changes code or files itself; it only proposes work.
Every proposal names the Notes Files stock it aims to raise and says how it would be checked.
It reads the Notes Files stock and the ticket queue only.
steps: 1. Once a day, read the Notes Files stock (notes_files) and the notes files added in the last day.
2. Compare with the day before; if the stock did not rise, propose one change that would add notes files, naming the stock it aims to raise.
3. Publish the proposal as a work.proposed event for the Supervisor to put to the owner; publish nothing if there is nothing to propose.

I've declared the **Notes Improver** Universal Machine. It is unconfirmed, so it will not run until you confirm it, and it costs nothing until then.

- **What it does:** once a day at 09:00, it reads the Notes Files stock and, if the count did not rise, proposes one change that would add notes files. It never changes files itself.
- **Cost as drafted:** about one turn a day on Haiku, roughly $0.03 a day.
- **Expected effect:** the Notes Files stock rises, judged over 7 days after it starts. The expectation is a draft until you confirm.
- **Guesses to check:** the time (09:00) and time zone (America/Los_Angeles) are my guesses, since you did not choose them. The event it publishes, `work.proposed`, is also a guess and has no listener yet.

Still open from before: keep or drop the `notes_files.count` instrument (it is a draft and expires in 24 hours), and the three answers I asked for on the daily loop.
